interactions.summary: A student presses whether enlightenment in the poem must result in good works, Jiang says Dante's path already includes learning and inquiry rather than mere inwardness, and he postpones the concrete answer about the pilgrim's deeds until the class finishes the Comedy.

A student asks whether faith can simply be treated as a hypothesis, and Jiang rejects that equivalence by saying hypotheses can be disproven while faith is the basic assumption from which everything else must proceed.

A student says modern people now believe in money, power, science, and AI more than God, and Jiang answers with his closing formula that Dante can reactivate imagination and restore the faith needed for the highest hope in a world marked by war.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student diagnosis and Jiang closing answer

claims.claim: The student insists that the highest hope cannot be reduced to inward meditation and must involve concrete good works.
Jiang answers that Dante's path already includes learning, debate, and inquiry rather than quietist withdrawal.
Jiang says the class cannot yet judge what good works the fictional pilgrim has done because the reading has not reached the end of the Comedy.
Jiang rejects the equation of faith with hypothesis because a hypothesis can be proven wrong, whereas faith is the starting assumption from which all further reasoning must come.
A student diagnoses the present as an age in which people believe in money, power, science, and AI more readily than in God, and therefore lose faith, hope, and love.
Jiang's closing answer is that widespread reading of Dante would activate imagination, restore faith, and help people achieve the highest hope and their true potential.
claims.temporal_scope: Normative and predictive claim stated on 2026-06-17.

claims.claim: Jiang explicitly dates the lecture's political horizon by describing the present as a world of war in which Donald Trump is president.

signature_moments.moment: Faith is distinguished from hypothesis by becoming the assumption from which everything else must unfold.
signature_moments.source_phrase: faith is is the assumption the thing from which everything must come
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the most compact late definition of faith in the whole packet sequence.

signature_moments.moment: The crisis of modernity is named as misplaced belief in money, power, science, and AI rather than in God, hope, and love.
signature_moments.source_phrase: people right now they don't believe in god most of them believe in money the power the science the ai
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the packet its sharpest contemporary diagnosis and ties Dante study to a civilizational emergency.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang's path forward is not technocratic reform or personal guru-following but collective reading that reactivates imagination and true selfhood.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the answer is not in me the answer is in you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the closing exhortation of the lecture and the strongest bridge from textual interpretation to public mission.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's late-lecture formula for faith as the basic premise from which the pursuit of highest hope and truth begins, unlike a revisable hypothesis.
The salvific end that requires faith and, in Jiang's closing rhetoric, becomes reachable through reactivated imagination and reading Dante.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 Jiang closes the lecture by tying the faith discussion to a contemporary political and civilizational diagnosis: amid war and a Trump presidency, Dante is offered as a way to reactivate imagination and restore hope.

uncertainty_notes.note: The claim that reading Dante will make people better and restore the path forward is a closing exhortation and should be preserved as Jiang's rhetorical prescription rather than as a tested causal finding.
